skill.name: biomni
skill.description: Run multi-step biomedical research workflows across genomics, drug discovery, molecular biology, and clinical analysis with the Biomni autonomous agent.
skill.summary: Plan, execute, and document biomedical analyses with an autonomous research agent.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most scanner hits are Markdown formatting, placeholder credentials, documentation links, or fixed subprocess calls. Confirmed issues include credential exposure, unsafe secret storage, generated-code injection, unescaped HTML, unpinned package execution, and full-privilege LLM code execution.

remediation.issue: Biomni executes LLM-generated code with full host privileges.
remediation.suggestion: Require an isolated container or virtual machine with restricted filesystem, network, process, and credential access before running agent tasks.

remediation.issue: Custom data paths are inserted into generated Python source.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid source generation or serialize paths with a safe literal encoder. Pass values as arguments and test malicious quotes and newlines.

remediation.issue: Setup and troubleshooting flows expose or weakly store API keys.
remediation.suggestion: Use hidden input, never print secret values, prefer a secret manager, and create local credential files with owner-only permissions.

remediation.issue: HTML reports embed conversation content and titles without escaping.
remediation.suggestion: Use a maintained Markdown renderer with HTML disabled or sanitize all generated HTML with an allow-list policy.

remediation.issue: The MCP example automatically executes an unpinned registry package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited package version and integrity value. Require explicit approval before installation and provide only narrowly scoped credentials.

semantic_findings.title: Unsandboxed LLM-Generated Code Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill states that Biomni executes LLM-generated code with full system privileges. Prompt or data manipulation could therefore become arbitrary host code execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly states full-privilege generated-code execution and describes generation and execution as standard agent behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Custom Path Enables Generated Python Injection
semantic_findings.description: A user-supplied data path is interpolated without escaping into generated Python source. The setup script then executes that source.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: A path containing quotes and newlines can break the Python string, insert statements, and reach the immediate subprocess execution.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The converter concatenates untrusted message text into tags and code blocks without HTML escaping or sanitization.

content.value_statement: Complex biomedical analyses require coordinated reasoning, data access, and reproducible reporting. Biomni guides an autonomous agent through these multi-step research workflows.
actual_capabilities: Decomposes biomedical questions into multi-step tasks and executes them through the Biomni A1 agent.
Supports CRISPR design, single-cell analysis, GWAS interpretation, ADMET prediction, and clinical genomics research.
Uses an approximately 11 GB biomedical data lake that downloads on first use.
Configures Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure, Google, Groq, AWS Bedrock, or custom LLM endpoints.
Connects external biomedical tools through Model Context Protocol configuration.
Saves conversation histories and formats them as Markdown or HTML research reports.
limitations: Biomni executes LLM-generated code with host privileges unless users provide isolation.
Operation requires the external Biomni package, provider credentials, network access, and substantial local storage.
Biomedical results require expert review and are not validated medical diagnoses or treatment recommendations.
The included report script does not create PDF files and falls back to HTML.

use_cases.title: Design Molecular Screens
use_cases.description: Develop CRISPR screening strategies, candidate priorities, controls, and validation plans for a defined phenotype.

use_cases.title: Analyze Omics Data
use_cases.description: Plan quality control, clustering, differential expression, pathway analysis, and interpretation for genomics datasets.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Translational Evidence
use_cases.description: Combine variants, phenotypes, pathways, and drug evidence to generate reviewable research hypotheses.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Gene
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize the known function of [gene] and list major associated diseases. Cite the databases used and identify uncertain claims.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Expression Groups
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [dataset path] for differential expression between [groups]. Report quality checks, significant genes, methods, and limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CRISPR Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CRISPR knockout screen for [phenotype] in [cell type]. Define controls, library strategy, prioritization criteria, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Causal Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate [GWAS file], [single-cell dataset], and [pathway constraints] to prioritize causal genes. Explain each processing step and uncertainty.

output_examples.input: Prioritize genes for an autophagy CRISPR screen in HEK293 cells.
output: Ranked gene candidates with pathway and essentiality evidence.
Screen controls, selection strategy, and expected technical limitations.
Validation experiments for the strongest candidates.

output_examples.input: Interpret significant variants from a disease GWAS summary file.
output: Enriched pathways and plausible disease mechanisms.
Uncertainty notes and recommended follow-up analyses.

output_examples.input: Compare ADMET properties for a small set of candidate compounds.
output: A comparative property summary for absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity.
Risk flags, evidence limitations, and priorities for experimental testing.

best_practices: Run Biomni inside an isolated environment and review generated code before execution.
Use deidentified data, least-privilege credentials, and approved provider configurations.
Set task constraints, timeouts, and iteration limits while preserving sources and conversation history.
anti_patterns: Do not run autonomous generated code on a sensitive production host.
Do not print credentials or store them in broadly readable plaintext files.
Do not treat generated biomedical conclusions as validated clinical guidance.

faq.question: What does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires Python, the Biomni package, an LLM provider credential, network access, and approximately 11 GB of storage.

faq.question: Which LLM providers are supported?
faq.answer: The documentation covers Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Google Gemini, Groq, AWS Bedrock, and custom endpoints.

faq.question: Does Biomni execute code?
faq.answer: Yes. Biomni generates and executes analysis code, so use a sandbox and inspect sensitive workflows.

faq.question: Can it analyze local datasets?
faq.answer: Yes. Prompts can reference local dataset paths, subject to Biomni dependencies, formats, and available resources.

faq.question: Does it generate PDF reports?
faq.answer: Biomni can save conversation history as PDF. The included helper script only produces Markdown or HTML.

faq.question: Can results support clinical decisions?
faq.answer: Results can support research review, but qualified experts must validate them before clinical or laboratory use.
